assessments.reasoning: The publisher-governing acquisition came from GNU’s fdl-1.2.txt. Its 20,394-byte body has the connector-reported SHA-256 2652c22ba086f92e55ae4a9f9c890ad4766ffd7814a73d318e22a597edf857a4, matching the claim’s provenance. The four pinned ranges locate the opening permission [181,303), the work-notice definition [1478,2073), the copying conditions [6267,7003), and the Addendum [19093,20394). Their different subjects resolve the apparent tension between permission to modify a covered work and the restriction on changing the license document.

limitations: The claim covers the complete pinned publisher plaintext. The two GNU acquisitions deliver the same publisher bytes and provide one source of authority.
A work’s authorized notice supplies its edition choice and feature designations. The cases below are hypothetical.
reasoning: The opening permission in GNU’s version 1.2 plaintext expressly allows everyone to copy and distribute the license document verbatim and bars changes to it. Section 1 defines the covered work through a notice placed by its copyright holder. Section 2 governs copies of that work. It requires reproduction of the license, copyright notices and applicable work notice, forbids added conditions and technical barriers to reading or further copying, and permits compensation.
